newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris posts 13 percent rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris posts 13 percent rise in profits.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos. Inc. said Wednesday that its first-quarter profits rose 13 percent to record levels on the strength of its domestic and international tobacco operations and its North American food business.

The company said its net income for the three months ended March 31 expanded to a record $1.77 billion, or 73 cents a share, from $1.57 billion, or 63 cents a share, a year earlier. The per-share figures reflect a three-for-one-stock split in March.
Philip Morris, which markets Miller beer and Kraft packaged foods as well as Marlboro cigarettes, said revenues grew to $18.2 billion from $17.5 billion.
"Performance was robust despite the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against key foreign currencies," Chairman Geoffrey C. Bible said in a statement.
"Although we will have to continue to contend with the strengthening of the U.S. dollar, the volume, market share and earnings fundamentals of our businesses remain powerful."
The company, whose cigarette brands include Virginia Slims, Benson & Hedges and Lark, said pretax operating income for the domestic tobacco business grew 11 percent to $1.1 billion.
Pretax operating income at the international tobacco business rose 15 percent to $1.3 billion on the growing overseas popularity of American-style cigarettes, it added.
The North American food business -- whose brands also include Post and Nabisco cereals, Oscar Mayer meats and Kraft and Velveeta cheese -- saw its operating income rise 10 percent to $743 million.
Philip Morris's stock jumped $3.125 to $42 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most actively traded issue.

The stock rise was partially influenced by separate reports that tobacco companies are negotiating with state attorneys general and plaintiffs' lawyers on a possible settlement of massive litigation against the industry.
